Legs.Subject: FixedVector3.MoveToward's boundary identities, asserted EXACTLY over eight segments — axis-aligned, diagonal, negative, mixed-sign and one separated by a single raw unit: a zero step returns the current point unchanged, a step equal to the remaining distance and every larger step return the TARGET itself rather than a point near it, and a degenerate segment whose endpoints coincide returns that point. The negative-step refusal is asserted by exception type AND by the parameter name it reports.

an INTERMEDIATE step, at six fractions of each segment's own length, satisfies three independent statements: what remains of the segment never grows, so the step cannot overshoot; the distance actually travelled is the distance asked for; and the travelled vector's cross product with the whole segment vanishes, so the point stays ON the segment rather than merely near the right distance. The three together are what a transposition of current and target, a dropped normalization, a negated step or a divide by the wrong length each fail — the first two of those are invisible to any one of the statements alone.
the travelled distance and the on-segment test
Legs.Against: the step the subject was handed and zero
Legs.Shared: FixedVector3.Length and FixedVector3.Cross — the IDENTICAL members the subject itself reaches through, since the subject divides by the very Length this claim measures with. A defect INSIDE Length that scaled every measurement alike would move the subject and this claim's expectation together and could not be caught here; Length's own agreement with an exact reference is vector.length-vs-oracle's statement, not this one's. What this claim does catch is everything ABOVE the norm — the early return, the operand order, the sign, and which vector is divided by which length.

Legs.Subject: ENVELOPE: the two interpolation statements carry TOLERANCES rather than exact equality, because the step runs through a fixed-point divide, a scale and a norm and each rounds. The tolerances are stated from the representation — one part in 256 of the separation plus a raw unit for the distance, one part in 64 plus 256 raw units for the cross product — and are not tuned against observed output, so they bound gross structural defects and deliberately do not pin the last-unit rounding of the interpolating path. A correction to that rounding is expected to pass this law unchanged; a law that pinned it would belong to FixedQ4816's divide and scale rather than here.

FixedQ4816.MoveToward's boundary identities, asserted EXACTLY over seven segments — increasing, decreasing, negative-range, mixed-sign and one degenerate: a zero step returns the current value unchanged, a step equal to the remaining distance and every larger step return the TARGET itself, and a degenerate segment whose endpoints coincide returns that point. The negative-step refusal is asserted by exception type AND by the parameter name it reports.
the distance travelled by an INTERMEDIATE step, at six fractions of each segment's own length, and what remains of the segment afterward
Legs.Against: the step the subject was handed and the segment's own separation
Legs.Shared: FixedQ4816.Abs — the identical member MoveToward's own early-return branch reaches through (it compares Abs(delta) against maxDelta before ever computing the moved point). Both identities are EXACT rather than tolerance-bounded, unlike the vector law's counterpart: the scalar path has no divide or normalize between the compare and the add, so nothing is rounded. What this claim catches is everything ABOVE Abs — an overshoot, an undershoot, or a step applied against the wrong operand.

Legs.Subject: the direction the intermediate step moved
Legs.Against: the sign of the segment's own displacement
Legs.Shared: FixedQ4816.Sign, over the same raw Value comparison substrate MoveToward's own delta > Zero branch reduces to — a member MoveToward's body never calls directly, so a transposed current/target or a negated step is caught by reading the moved point's own displacement rather than by re-executing the subject's branch.

Legs.Subject: the landing verdict and, on a non-landing step, each axis's movement sign, at eight carrier-extreme segments (each axis alone at the opposing raw extremes with the other two held at zero, plus all three together) and five step sizes including a single raw unit and the largest representable step
Legs.Against: Oracles.MoveTowardVerdict, whose per-axis displacement and squared-distance comparison are formed entirely in BigInteger with no wrap or narrowing at any width — never the subject's own componentwise target-minus-current, which is exactly what wraps at these endpoints

Legs.Subject: the never-overshoot bound on a non-landing step's travelled distance
Legs.Against: maxDelta plus a small fixed tolerance
Legs.Shared: FixedVector3.Length and the subtraction operator, the same members vector.move-toward-boundaries-and-segment's own travelled-distance leg reaches through; a defect INSIDE Length that scaled every measurement alike would move the subject and this bound together

Legs.Subject: ENVELOPE: an axis is allowed to report NO movement even on a non-landing step, because the fixed-point unit direction can round a tiny per-axis share of maxDelta to zero (the all-three-extreme segment at maxDelta raw 1 is exactly this case) — the leg only refuses movement against the oracle's sign, never a rounded-to-zero movement.
the exact resulting raw at both orderings of the opposing carrier extremes and five step sizes including a single raw unit and the largest representable step
Legs.Against: Oracles.MoveTowardRaw, whose displacement is formed entirely in BigInteger with no wrap at any width — never the subject's own target-minus-current, which is exactly what wraps at these endpoints

Legs.Subject: both emitters are PURE: each produces byte-identical text on two calls, and running one between two calls of the other does not disturb it. That is the property the type's own remarks claim — no wall clock, no unseeded source, an unchanged host giving byte-identical output every run — and it is the property a generated artifact committed to the tree depends on, since a drifting emitter makes every regeneration a spurious diff. A shared StringBuilder, a static cursor or a re-seeded generator all fail it.

the emitted text carries the LIVE values it claims to read: FixedQ4816.Atan2HalfPiQ61 and PiQ61 appear in the generated source as the invariant decimals the type currently holds, and the emitted vector file carries the raw value the live FixedQ4816.Sin returns for one. That is the whole design claim this file makes for itself — every table and coefficient read from the live type by NAME rather than transcribed — so a constant referenced by the wrong name, or a vector file that emitted its inputs without the host's answers, stops satisfying it.

ENVELOPE, and it is the reason this is a purity-and-transcription law rather than a port-agreement one: NOTHING here executes the emitted Rust or compares it against the committed artifact, so this law says nothing about whether the ported algorithm still agrees with its host bit for bit. That statement needs the emitted text compiled and run against known-answer vectors, which no gate in this repository performs today — the stage that compared emitted text against what is committed left the build with Puck.Post, and the type's own remarks say so. OWED: a runner that regenerates and diffs, or that executes the port. Until one exists, drift in the PORT is caught only by a human regenerating and reading the diff, and only drift in the emitter's own determinism and constant references is caught here.
